newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia aircraft firm to raise some 2.8 trln rph.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia aircraft firm to raise some 2.8 trln rph.

text.p: Indonesia's privately-owned aircraft firm PT Dua Satu Tiga Puluh (DSTP), chaired by President Suharto, said on Thursday it planned to raise around 2.8 trillion rupiah through a public offering until 2006 to finance a $2.0 billion aircraft project.

"The proceeds from the offering will be used to help finance PT IPTN's N-2130 jet aircraft," DSTP president director Saadilah Mursid, who is also Cabinet Secretary, said in a public presentation at the Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam).
DSTP's board of commissioners include President Suharto as president and former vice presidents, Umar Wirahadikusumah and Sudharmono, as members.
Mursid said the offering was considered to be special as there was no intention for the time being to list the shares on either the Jakarta or the Surabaya stock exchanges.
"In the long term, it might be necessary to list the shares on the Jakarta or Surabaya stock exchange. But for the time being there is no such a plan," Mursid said.
Responding to a question on the mechanism of trading in the shares, Mursid said the firm was still studying the matter.
He said DSTP expected to sell the shares for the time being only to Indonesian citizens and not to foreigners.
Mursid also said there would be no underwriter for the offering. The offering was expected to be a success even without an underwriting agreement, he added.
DSTP expected to start holding public presentations throughout the country to promote the offering later this month and start the sale of shares later in the year, Mursid said.
The company will offer 774,398 shares with a nominal value of 2.3 million rupiah and an offering price of 2.4 million rupiah per share.
It will also offer 400,000 shares, with each share divisable into 460 units, each with a nominal price of 5,000 rupiah and offering price of 5,500 rupiah, the firm said in a brief statement.
DSTP's Director Giri Hadihardjono said the firm expected to secure some 600 billion rupiah in 1997, but said the offering was expected to go on until around the year 2006.
Mursid said DSTP, which signed a cooperation agreement with IPTN last October, would receive revenues such as royalties from the sale of the N-2130 jets.
Giri said at the presentation that the 130-passenger jet was expected to cost some $2 billion from the feasibility study to certification.

State-owned aircraft manufacturer PT Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara (IPTN) had started the project and expected to roll out the prototype in 2002 and start commercial production in 2005, Mursid said.
"We expect IPTN to touch the break-even-point with the production of 326th (N-2130), which is expected to be achieved in the year 2013," Mursid said.
The aircraft and advance technology development firm has total paid-up capital of around 900 billion rupiah, Mursid said.
The firm, set up in early last year, currently employees less than 25 people, the firm's law consultant firm said at the presentation.
